However, this is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, contact your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco products. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning surgery, or will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these situations increase the risk of blood clots, especially if you are taking an estrogen-containing product. Limit your time in the sun, and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, potentially affecting their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing inaccurate results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular Monitoring: While taking this medication, regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Lifestyle Changes: Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises (e.g., reading or solving crossword puzzles) may help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, engage in weight-bearing exercises, quit smoking, limit alcohol consumption, and eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
